question: Electron-volt is a unit of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**energy.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The electron volt is the unit of **energy**__ commonly used in atomic and nuclear physics.

 __
 
• The amount of energy gained by the charge of a single electron moved across an electric potential difference of 1 volt is called an **electron volt.**
 
• It is commonly used in atomic and nuclear physics applications.
 
• The symbol of electron volt is **eV.**
 
• **1eV = 1.602×10-19 J**
 
• **1eV = 1.602 × 10−12 erg**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Other units of energy are:
 
 
• **Joule** is the SI unit of Energy.

 
 
• The unit Joule is named after the English physicist James Prescott Joule.
 
• Kg⋅m²⋅s⁻² is the SI base unit of Joule.
 
 
 
• **The calorie **is a unit of energy commonly used in nutrition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Watt** is the SI unit of Power.

 
 
• The unit watt is named after scientist James Watt.
 
 
 
• **Volt** is the SI unit of potential difference.
 
• **Ampere** is the SI unit of current.
